assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental demonstration and quantitative physical description of long-range electron tunneling through protein matrices, with distance and driving-force dependence, tunneling pathways and hopping. It grounds respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer in physical mechanism, which is the kind of principle-level biochemistry I value most.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear pair behind the Ru-modified protein and photochemical triggering work. Related theory (Marcus, already recognized) and pathway models by others (Beratan, Onuchic) are not credited here and may complicate the story. Two names is a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation across many proteins and independent groups; the concepts are textbook and stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1992 Marcus prize may make the committee view the experimental advance as a continuation rather than a new discovery.
Tunneling-pathway versus hopping interpretations are still debated in detail.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structure and mechanism of nitrogenase, the enzyme enabling biological N2 reduction through the unique FeMo cofactor, with the central interstitial carbon and the electron/proton delivery cycle. A fundamental bioinorganic mechanism of great chemical and global importance, and one where structure and kinetics must meet.
assessment.attribution: Rees provided the structural foundation, Dean the genetics and cofactor assembly, Seefeldt the kinetic and mechanistic framework. Einsle (high-resolution structure, carbide) and Ribbe (cofactor biosynthesis) also have strong claims, so the three-name limit forces a hard choice and priority is not obviously settled.
assessment.maturity: Structures have been confirmed repeatedly over three decades, including recent cryo-EM of turnover states; however the catalytic mechanism and the substrate-binding site remain only partly resolved.
uncertainties: The mechanism of N2 reduction at the cofactor is not fully settled, so the discovery could be viewed as still maturing.
Allocation among Rees, Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a general route to radical and excited-state reactivity under mild conditions and is now routine in synthesis and industry. The impact is broad and mechanistically rich, though my own expertise is less in synthetic methodology.
assessment.attribution: The decisive 2008-2009 reports came from MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson, with antecedents from Fukuzumi, Kellogg and Cano-Yelo and parallel work from Nicewicz, Konig and Melchiorre. MacMillan is already a laureate (2021), which may bear on the committee's willingness; the credit is diffuse across seven names.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed and widely adopted over fifteen years; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority is spread over many groups and earlier photochemical precedents.
MacMillan's prior prize may argue for a different trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs enables room-temperature, radiation-damage-free structures and time-resolved structural movies of reactions, including photosystem II and light-driven proteins. It makes dynamic biochemical mechanisms visible, closely aligned with combining time-resolved methods and structures.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof of principle and method development, Fromme the membrane protein and photosystem work, Schlichting the time-resolved enzyme and photoreceptor studies. Hajdu was an originator of the concept and I am uncertain of his current status; allocation among these remains open.
assessment.maturity: Method is well established at several facilities, though many time-resolved results are still being scrutinized for interpretation; reasonably mature for the method, less so for specific mechanistic outcomes.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should honor the method or its chemical applications.
Hajdu's status and credit are uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer defines how electrons and protons move together in enzymes and catalysts, central to respiration, photosynthesis and fuel-forming electrocatalysis. Importance is high and close to my own field of proton transfer in cytochrome oxidase.
assessment.attribution: Meyer introduced early PCET concepts, Mayer the thermochemical and concerted-pathway framework, Hammes-Schiffer the theory, and Nocera the molecular systems. This is a line of work rather than one attributable discovery, which makes a fair three-person configuration hard.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are well accepted, but quantitative generality across systems is still evolving.
uncertainties: Candidacy rests on a body of work rather than a single discovery.
Meyer's long-standing contributions versus more recent theory and catalysis work could split credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase to give stoichiometry, topology and ligand binding of intact complexes including membrane proteins, complementing structural biology.
assessment.attribution: Robinson, Heck and Chait are the leading developers and appliers; Loo and Gross have earlier claims, and the electrospray roots were already recognized in 2002, which complicates novelty.
assessment.maturity: Mature and broadly adopted, with extensive independent validation.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for electrospray ionization.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a transformative reaction for making amines in pharmaceuticals and materials, with well-understood catalytic mechanism and ligand design.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic method; Kosugi and Migita reported earlier tin-amide couplings. Credit assignment between pioneers and generalizers is a clear priority question, and Pd cross-coupling was recognized in 2010.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of industrial use; timely or even late.
uncertainties: Novelty relative to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Priority of Kosugi and Migita; Migita is not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural and mechanistic dissection of the spliceosome, with cryo-EM revealing how a large RNA-protein machine assembles and catalyzes two-step splicing. It exemplifies methods making complex biochemical mechanisms visible.
assessment.attribution: Luhrmann for biochemical purification and compositional work, Shi and Stark for the structures; the many contributing groups (Nagai, Lührmann, Shi, Stark) make a three-person limit and allocation delicate.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed across species, but the field is still resolving dynamics and chemical details of catalysis.
uncertainties: This may be viewed as molecular biology or structural biology more than chemistry.
Other structural contributors such as Nagai are not among the credited names.
